scenario.ms: Penghutang awal RM12,000. Jualan kredit RM45,000. Tunai diterima RM38,000. Diskaun diberi RM1,200. Pulangan masuk RM800. Hutang lapuk dihapus kira RM500.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete the control account.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan akaun kawalan.

scenario.en: Opening debtors RM9,000. Credit sales RM52,000. Cash received RM44,000. Discount allowed RM1,500. Returns inwards RM1,000. Bad debts written off RM800.
scenario.ms: Penghutang awal RM9,000. Jualan kredit RM52,000. Tunai diterima RM44,000. Diskaun diberi RM1,500. Pulangan masuk RM1,000. Hutang lapuk dihapus kira RM800.

explanation.en: 9,000 + 52,000 = 61,000, less 44,000 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 800 = 47,300, leaving 13,700. Every one of those four reduces what customers owe.
explanation.ms: 9,000 + 52,000 = 61,000, tolak 44,000 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 800 = 47,300, tinggal 13,700. Keempat-empatnya mengurangkan hutang pelanggan.

prompt.en: Only the opening balance is given. Build the whole control account.
prompt.ms: Hanya baki awal diberi. Bina keseluruhan akaun kawalan.

scenario.en: Opening creditors RM8,000. Credit purchases RM26,000. Payments to suppliers RM22,000. Discount received RM900. Returns outwards RM600.
scenario.ms: Pemiutang awal RM8,000. Belian kredit RM26,000. Bayaran kepada pembekal RM22,000. Diskaun diterima RM900. Pulangan keluar RM600.

explanation.en: 8,000 + 26,000 − 22,000 − 900 − 600 = 10,500. The creditors account runs the same shape as the debtors one — only the meaning of each line flips.
explanation.ms: 8,000 + 26,000 − 22,000 − 900 − 600 = 10,500. Akaun pemiutang berjalan dengan bentuk yang sama seperti penghutang — hanya maksud setiap baris yang berbalik.

title.en: Six Errors the Trial Balance Cannot See
title.ms: Enam Kesilapan Yang Imbangan Duga Tidak Nampak

prompt.en: A trial balance that agrees is not proof the books are right. Six errors keep both sides equal and slip straight through: OMISSION (left out entirely), COMMISSION (right kind of account, wrong person), PRINCIPLE (wrong class of account — an asset treated as an expense), ORIGINAL ENTRY (the same wrong figure used on both sides), COMPLETE REVERSAL (debit and credit swapped), and COMPENSATING (two errors of the same size cancelling out). Only a one-sided error — a missing posting, or a column added up wrongly — makes the trial balance disagree, and that is what a suspense account is for.
prompt.ms: Imbangan duga yang seimbang bukan bukti buku itu betul. Enam kesilapan mengekalkan kedua-dua belah sama dan lolos terus: PENINGGALAN (tertinggal sepenuhnya), KOMISEN (jenis akaun betul, orang salah), PRINSIP (kelas akaun salah — aset dianggap belanja), CATATAN ASAL (angka salah yang sama digunakan di kedua-dua belah), TERBALIK SEPENUHNYA (debit dan kredit bertukar), dan SALING MENGIMBANGI (dua kesilapan sama besar yang membatalkan). Hanya kesilapan sebelah — catatan yang tertinggal, atau lajur yang salah campur — membuat imbangan duga tidak seimbang, dan itulah gunanya akaun penyelesaian.

prompt.en: A credit sale to Ali was never entered in the books at all. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Jualan kredit kepada Ali langsung tidak dimasukkan ke dalam buku. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: Nothing was recorded on either side, so the trial balance still agrees.
explanation.ms: Tiada apa direkod di kedua-dua belah, jadi imbangan duga masih seimbang.

prompt.en: A credit sale to Ali was posted to Abu's account instead. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Jualan kredit kepada Ali dicatat ke akaun Abu sebaliknya. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: The right TYPE of account was used — a debtor — just the wrong person. That is commission, not principle.
explanation.ms: JENIS akaun yang betul digunakan — penghutang — cuma orang yang salah. Itu komisen, bukan prinsip.

prompt.en: The purchase of a van was debited to the Purchases account. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Pembelian van didebitkan ke akaun Belian. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: A non-current asset was treated as an expense — a whole different CLASS of account. That is principle.
explanation.ms: Aset bukan semasa dianggap belanja — KELAS akaun yang berbeza sama sekali. Itu prinsip.

prompt.en: A sale of RM540 was entered as RM450 in both the sales account and the customer's account. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Jualan RM540 dimasukkan sebagai RM450 dalam kedua-dua akaun jualan dan akaun pelanggan. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: The wrong figure was taken from the source document, then used consistently on both sides.
explanation.ms: Angka salah diambil daripada dokumen sumber, kemudian digunakan secara konsisten di kedua-dua belah.

prompt.en: Cash paid to a supplier was debited to Cash and credited to the supplier's account. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Tunai dibayar kepada pembekal didebitkan ke Tunai dan dikreditkan ke akaun pembekal. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: Both entries are on exactly the wrong sides. Correcting it needs DOUBLE the amount — once to cancel, once to record it properly.
explanation.ms: Kedua-dua catatan berada di sebelah yang salah. Membetulkannya perlu DUA KALI ganda amaun — sekali untuk batal, sekali untuk rekod dengan betul.

prompt.en: The sales account was overcast by RM100 and the purchases account was also overcast by RM100. Which error is this?
prompt.ms: Akaun jualan tercampur lebih RM100 dan akaun belian juga tercampur lebih RM100. Kesilapan apakah ini?

explanation.en: One error on each side, the same size, cancelling each other out. The totals agree even though both accounts are wrong.
explanation.ms: Satu kesilapan di setiap belah, sama besar, saling membatalkan. Jumlah seimbang walaupun kedua-dua akaun salah.

prompt.en: A credit sale was omitted from the books entirely. Will the trial balance still agree?
prompt.ms: Jualan kredit tertinggal sepenuhnya daripada buku. Adakah imbangan duga masih seimbang?

options: Yes — the trial balance still agrees
No — the trial balance will not agree
options_ms: Tidak — imbangan duga tidak akan seimbang

items.answer: Yes — the trial balance still agrees

explanation.en: Nothing was entered on either side, so both totals are equally understated.
explanation.ms: Tiada apa dimasukkan di kedua-dua belah, jadi kedua-dua jumlah kurang sama banyak.

prompt.en: The sales account was undercast by RM400. Will the trial balance still agree?
prompt.ms: Akaun jualan tercampur kurang RM400. Adakah imbangan duga masih seimbang?

options: Yes — the trial balance still agrees
No — the trial balance will not agree
options_ms: Tidak — imbangan duga tidak akan seimbang

items.answer: No — the trial balance will not agree

explanation.en: Only the credit side is wrong, so the two totals differ by RM400 — a suspense account is needed.
explanation.ms: Hanya sebelah kredit yang salah, jadi kedua-dua jumlah berbeza RM400 — akaun penyelesaian diperlukan.

prompt.en: When the trial balance will not agree, the difference is parked in a suspense account so the books can carry on. Each one-sided error found is then corrected with a journal entry: the real account gets the entry it should have had, and the suspense account takes the other side. When every error has been found, the suspense account is empty.
prompt.ms: Apabila imbangan duga tidak seimbang, perbezaannya diletakkan dalam akaun penyelesaian supaya buku boleh diteruskan. Setiap kesilapan sebelah yang dijumpai kemudian dibetulkan dengan catatan jurnal: akaun sebenar mendapat catatan yang sepatutnya, dan akaun penyelesaian mengambil sebelah lagi. Apabila semua kesilapan dijumpai, akaun penyelesaian menjadi kosong.

prompt.en: The trial balance debit total exceeds the credit total by RM500. The suspense account opens with a balance on the...
prompt.ms: Jumlah debit imbangan duga melebihi jumlah kredit sebanyak RM500. Akaun penyelesaian dibuka dengan baki di sebelah...

explanation.en: The credit side is short, so RM500 of credit is added to make the totals agree.
explanation.ms: Sebelah kredit kurang, jadi RM500 kredit ditambah untuk menyeimbangkan jumlah.

prompt.en: A trial balance shows a debit total of RM45,600 and a credit total of RM45,100. What amount goes into the suspense account?
prompt.ms: Imbangan duga menunjukkan jumlah debit RM45,600 dan jumlah kredit RM45,100. Berapakah amaun yang masuk ke akaun penyelesaian?

explanation.en: 45,600 − 45,100 = 500. The suspense account holds the difference until the errors are found.
explanation.ms: 45,600 − 45,100 = 500. Akaun penyelesaian memegang perbezaan sehingga kesilapan dijumpai.

prompt.en: Wages of RM250 were correctly credited to Bank but never debited to the Wages account. Record the correcting entry.
prompt.ms: Gaji RM250 dikreditkan dengan betul ke Bank tetapi tidak pernah didebitkan ke akaun Gaji. Rekod catatan pembetulan.

explanation.en: The Bank side was already right, so it is not touched. Wages gets the debit it was missing, and suspense supplies the other side.
explanation.ms: Sebelah Bank sudah betul, jadi ia tidak disentuh. Gaji mendapat debit yang tertinggal, dan penyelesaian membekalkan sebelah lagi.

prompt.en: The sales account was undercast by RM400. Record the correcting entry.
prompt.ms: Akaun jualan tercampur kurang RM400. Rekod catatan pembetulan.

explanation.en: Sales was understated, so it needs RM400 more credit. Suspense takes the matching debit.
explanation.ms: Jualan kurang dinyatakan, jadi ia perlu RM400 kredit lagi. Penyelesaian mengambil debit yang sepadan.

prompt.en: A van bought for RM12,000 by cheque was recorded as: Dr Purchases 12,000 / Cr Bank 12,000. Fix it.
prompt.ms: Van dibeli RM12,000 dengan cek direkod sebagai: Dt Belian 12,000 / Kt Bank 12,000. Betulkan.

explanation.en: An error of principle: the van is a non-current asset, not goods for resale. The Bank side was always right, and the trial balance never noticed.
explanation.ms: Kesilapan prinsip: van ialah aset bukan semasa, bukan barang untuk dijual semula. Sebelah Bank sentiasa betul, dan imbangan duga tidak pernah perasan.

prompt.en: Clearing a suspense account is a countdown: start with the difference it was opened with, take off each error as you correct it, and the account must finish at zero. If it does not, an error is still out there.
prompt.ms: Menyelesaikan akaun penyelesaian ialah kiraan menurun: mula dengan perbezaan yang membukanya, tolak setiap kesilapan sambil anda membetulkannya, dan akaun itu mesti berakhir pada sifar. Jika tidak, masih ada kesilapan di luar sana.

prompt.en: The corrections are listed. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Pembetulan sudah disenaraikan. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: The trial balance debit total exceeded the credit total by RM500, so a suspense account was opened. Two errors were then found: sales undercast by RM400, and discount received of RM100 never posted.
scenario.ms: Jumlah debit imbangan duga melebihi kredit sebanyak RM500, jadi akaun penyelesaian dibuka. Dua kesilapan kemudian dijumpai: jualan tercampur kurang RM400, dan diskaun diterima RM100 tidak pernah dicatat.

label.en: Less: sales undercast, now credited to Sales
label.ms: Tolak: jualan tercampur kurang, kini dikredit ke Jualan

explanation.en: 500 − 400 − 100 = 0. Both missing entries were credits, which is exactly why the credit side was short.
explanation.ms: 500 − 400 − 100 = 0. Kedua-dua catatan yang tertinggal ialah kredit, itulah sebabnya sebelah kredit kurang.

prompt.en: Two lines are missing. Clear the suspense account.
prompt.ms: Dua baris hilang. Selesaikan akaun penyelesaian.

scenario.en: The trial balance credit total exceeded the debit total by RM300, so a suspense account was opened. Purchases were undercast by RM200, and rent paid of RM100 was never posted to the Rent account.
scenario.ms: Jumlah kredit imbangan duga melebihi debit sebanyak RM300, jadi akaun penyelesaian dibuka. Belian tercampur kurang RM200, dan sewa dibayar RM100 tidak pernah dicatat ke akaun Sewa.

label.en: Less: purchases undercast, now debited to Purchases
label.ms: Tolak: belian tercampur kurang, kini didebit ke Belian

label.en: Less: rent now debited to Rent
label.ms: Tolak: sewa kini didebit ke Sewa

explanation.en: 300 − 200 − 100 = 0. This time the missing entries were both debits, so the debit side was the short one.
explanation.ms: 300 − 200 − 100 = 0. Kali ini catatan yang tertinggal kedua-duanya debit, jadi sebelah debit yang kurang.

prompt.en: Only the scenario is given. Work the whole suspense account.
prompt.ms: Hanya senario diberi. Kerjakan keseluruhan akaun penyelesaian.

scenario.en: The trial balance debit total exceeded the credit total by RM750, so a suspense account was opened. Sales were undercast by RM450, and discount received of RM300 was never posted.
scenario.ms: Jumlah debit imbangan duga melebihi kredit sebanyak RM750, jadi akaun penyelesaian dibuka. Jualan tercampur kurang RM450, dan diskaun diterima RM300 tidak pernah dicatat.

label.en: Less: sales undercast, now credited to Sales
label.ms: Tolak: jualan tercampur kurang, kini dikredit ke Jualan

explanation.en: 750 − 450 − 300 = 0. A suspense account that will not clear to zero means at least one error is still undiscovered.
explanation.ms: 750 − 450 − 300 = 0. Akaun penyelesaian yang tidak menjadi sifar bermakna sekurang-kurangnya satu kesilapan masih belum dijumpai.

prompt.en: Many small traders keep no double entry at all, so there is no income statement to read the profit from. It has to be reasoned out instead: capital is whatever the business owns minus what it owes (a Statement of Affairs), and any GROWTH in capital over the year must have come from profit. Two adjustments finish it — drawings are ADDED back, because money the owner took out was still profit earned; capital introduced is DEDUCTED, because that growth came from the owner's pocket, not from trading.
prompt.ms: Ramai peniaga kecil langsung tidak menyimpan catatan bergu, jadi tiada penyata pendapatan untuk membaca untung. Ia perlu ditaakul: modal ialah apa yang perniagaan miliki tolak apa yang dihutang (Penyata Hal Ehwal), dan sebarang PERTAMBAHAN modal sepanjang tahun mesti datang daripada untung. Dua pelarasan melengkapkannya — ambilan DITAMBAH semula, kerana wang yang diambil pemilik tetap untung yang diperoleh; modal dimasukkan DITOLAK, kerana pertambahan itu datang daripada poket pemilik, bukan daripada perniagaan.

prompt.en: A business has assets of RM45,000 and liabilities of RM12,000. What is the capital?
prompt.ms: Sebuah perniagaan mempunyai aset RM45,000 dan liabiliti RM12,000. Berapakah modalnya?

explanation.en: Capital = assets − liabilities = 45,000 − 12,000 = 33,000. The accounting equation, rearranged.
explanation.ms: Modal = aset − liabiliti = 45,000 − 12,000 = 33,000. Persamaan perakaunan, disusun semula.

prompt.en: Opening capital was RM25,000 and closing capital is RM33,000. There were no drawings and no capital introduced. What is the profit for the year?
prompt.ms: Modal awal RM25,000 dan modal akhir RM33,000. Tiada ambilan dan tiada modal dimasukkan. Berapakah untung bagi tahun itu?

explanation.en: 33,000 − 25,000 = 8,000. With nothing taken out or put in, the whole growth in capital is profit.
explanation.ms: 33,000 − 25,000 = 8,000. Tanpa apa-apa dikeluarkan atau dimasukkan, seluruh pertambahan modal ialah untung.

prompt.en: Opening capital RM25,000, closing capital RM33,000, drawings RM6,000. What is the profit for the year?
prompt.ms: Modal awal RM25,000, modal akhir RM33,000, ambilan RM6,000. Berapakah untung bagi tahun itu?

explanation.en: 33,000 − 25,000 + 6,000 = 14,000. The RM6,000 the owner took out was profit too — capital only looks smaller because it left.
explanation.ms: 33,000 − 25,000 + 6,000 = 14,000. RM6,000 yang diambil pemilik juga untung — modal hanya kelihatan kecil kerana ia telah keluar.

prompt.en: Opening capital RM25,000, closing capital RM40,000, drawings RM6,000, additional capital introduced RM5,000. What is the profit for the year?
prompt.ms: Modal awal RM25,000, modal akhir RM40,000, ambilan RM6,000, modal tambahan dimasukkan RM5,000. Berapakah untung bagi tahun itu?

explanation.en: 40,000 − 25,000 + 6,000 − 5,000 = 16,000. The RM5,000 came from the owner, not from trading, so it must come back out.
explanation.ms: 40,000 − 25,000 + 6,000 − 5,000 = 16,000. RM5,000 itu datang daripada pemilik, bukan daripada perniagaan, jadi ia mesti ditolak semula.

prompt.en: In the capital-comparison profit formula, drawings are...
prompt.ms: Dalam formula untung perbandingan modal, ambilan adalah...

explanation.en: Drawings shrank the closing capital, but the money was still profit the business earned. Add it back.
explanation.ms: Ambilan mengecilkan modal akhir, tetapi wang itu tetap untung yang diperoleh perniagaan. Tambah semula.

prompt.en: In the capital-comparison profit formula, additional capital introduced is...
prompt.ms: Dalam formula untung perbandingan modal, modal tambahan yang dimasukkan adalah...

explanation.en: It grew the capital without the business earning anything, so it must be stripped out before you can call the rest profit.
explanation.ms: Ia menambah modal tanpa perniagaan memperoleh apa-apa, jadi ia mesti dikeluarkan sebelum yang selebihnya boleh dipanggil untung.

prompt.en: Sort these balances into a Statement of Affairs, then work out the capital.
prompt.ms: Asingkan baki ini ke dalam Penyata Hal Ehwal, kemudian kira modalnya.

explanation.en: Assets 45,000 − liabilities 12,000 = capital 33,000. A statement of affairs is just a balance sheet built from whatever records survive.
explanation.ms: Aset 45,000 − liabiliti 12,000 = modal 33,000. Penyata hal ehwal hanyalah kunci kira-kira yang dibina daripada rekod yang masih ada.

prompt.en: Opening debtors RM9,000, closing debtors RM11,000, cash received from customers RM50,000. What were the credit sales?
prompt.ms: Penghutang awal RM9,000, penghutang akhir RM11,000, tunai diterima daripada pelanggan RM50,000. Berapakah jualan kredit?

explanation.en: 50,000 + 11,000 − 9,000 = 52,000. Reconstruct the control account: whatever is still owed at the end, plus what was collected, minus what was already owed at the start.
explanation.ms: 50,000 + 11,000 − 9,000 = 52,000. Bina semula akaun kawalan: apa yang masih dihutang di akhir, campur apa yang dikutip, tolak apa yang sudah dihutang di awal.

prompt.en: Opening creditors RM6,000, closing creditors RM8,000, payments to suppliers RM31,000. What were the credit purchases?
prompt.ms: Pemiutang awal RM6,000, pemiutang akhir RM8,000, bayaran kepada pembekal RM31,000. Berapakah belian kredit?

explanation.en: 31,000 + 8,000 − 6,000 = 33,000 — the same reconstruction, run on the creditors side.
explanation.ms: 31,000 + 8,000 − 6,000 = 33,000 — pembinaan semula yang sama, dijalankan di sebelah pemiutang.

prompt.en: The calculation always runs the same way: closing capital, take off opening capital to find the increase, add back drawings, then take off any capital introduced. What is left is the profit. Each rung below hides one more line.
prompt.ms: Pengiraan sentiasa berjalan sama: modal akhir, tolak modal awal untuk mencari pertambahan, tambah semula ambilan, kemudian tolak sebarang modal dimasukkan. Yang tinggal ialah untung. Setiap anak tangga di bawah menyembunyikan satu baris lagi.

prompt.en: The workings are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Kerja kira sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: Opening capital RM25,000, closing capital RM40,000, drawings RM6,000, additional capital introduced RM5,000.
scenario.ms: Modal awal RM25,000, modal akhir RM40,000, ambilan RM6,000, modal tambahan dimasukkan RM5,000.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Work out the profit.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Kira untungnya.

scenario.en: Opening capital RM40,000, closing capital RM58,000, drawings RM9,000, additional capital introduced RM4,000.
scenario.ms: Modal awal RM40,000, modal akhir RM58,000, ambilan RM9,000, modal tambahan dimasukkan RM4,000.

explanation.en: 18,000 + 9,000 − 4,000 = 23,000. Drawings up, capital introduced down — the two adjustments always pull in opposite directions.
explanation.ms: 18,000 + 9,000 − 4,000 = 23,000. Ambilan naik, modal dimasukkan turun — kedua-dua pelarasan sentiasa menarik ke arah bertentangan.

prompt.en: Only the closing capital is given. Work out the profit.
prompt.ms: Hanya modal akhir diberi. Kira untungnya.

scenario.en: Opening capital RM55,000, closing capital RM72,000, drawings RM12,000, additional capital introduced RM3,000.
scenario.ms: Modal awal RM55,000, modal akhir RM72,000, ambilan RM12,000, modal tambahan dimasukkan RM3,000.

explanation.en: 72,000 − 55,000 = 17,000 increase, then 17,000 + 12,000 − 3,000 = 26,000. Note the profit is far bigger than the capital growth — that is normal when the owner draws heavily.
explanation.ms: 72,000 − 55,000 = 17,000 pertambahan, kemudian 17,000 + 12,000 − 3,000 = 26,000. Perhatikan untung jauh lebih besar daripada pertambahan modal — itu biasa apabila pemilik banyak mengambil.

prompt.en: A club is not trading for profit, so its statements are renamed — but the accounting is the one you already know. The Receipts and Payments Account is simply a summarised cash book: every ringgit in and out, including equipment bought and subscriptions for other years. The Income and Expenditure Account is the club's income statement: only THIS year's revenue items, with accruals and prepayments applied exactly as in Stage 5. Profit becomes SURPLUS, loss becomes DEFICIT, and capital becomes the ACCUMULATED FUND.
prompt.ms: Kelab tidak berniaga untuk untung, jadi penyatanya dinamakan semula — tetapi perakaunannya sama seperti yang anda sudah tahu. Akaun Terimaan dan Pembayaran hanyalah buku tunai yang diringkaskan: setiap ringgit masuk dan keluar, termasuk peralatan dibeli dan yuran bagi tahun lain. Akaun Pendapatan dan Perbelanjaan ialah penyata pendapatan kelab: hanya item hasil bagi tahun INI, dengan terakru dan prabayar dikenakan sama seperti Tahap 5. Untung menjadi LEBIHAN, rugi menjadi DEFISIT, dan modal menjadi KUMPULAN WANG TERKUMPUL.

prompt.en: The club buys new sports equipment for RM4,000 cash. Where does the RM4,000 appear?
prompt.ms: Kelab membeli peralatan sukan baharu RM4,000 secara tunai. Di manakah RM4,000 itu muncul?

explanation.en: Cash left the club, so it belongs in the cash summary. The equipment is an asset, not a cost of the year — only its depreciation reaches the Income and Expenditure Account.
explanation.ms: Tunai keluar dari kelab, jadi ia masuk dalam ringkasan tunai. Peralatan ialah aset, bukan kos tahun ini — hanya susut nilainya sampai ke Akaun Pendapatan dan Perbelanjaan.

prompt.en: Depreciation of the club's equipment for the year is RM1,200. Where does it appear?
prompt.ms: Susut nilai peralatan kelab bagi tahun ini RM1,200. Di manakah ia muncul?

explanation.en: No cash moves for depreciation, so the cash summary never sees it — but it is a genuine cost of the year.
explanation.ms: Tiada tunai bergerak untuk susut nilai, jadi ringkasan tunai tidak melihatnya — tetapi ia kos sebenar bagi tahun ini.

prompt.en: A member pays next year's subscription early. In which account is the cash recorded?
prompt.ms: Seorang ahli membayar yuran tahun depan lebih awal. Dalam akaun manakah tunai itu direkod?

explanation.en: The cash really arrived, so the cash summary records all of it. It is not income of THIS year, so it is kept out of the Income and Expenditure Account.
explanation.ms: Tunai itu benar-benar masuk, jadi ringkasan tunai merekod semuanya. Ia bukan pendapatan tahun INI, jadi ia dikecualikan daripada Akaun Pendapatan dan Perbelanjaan.

prompt.en: In a club, what is capital called?
prompt.ms: Dalam kelab, apakah nama bagi modal?

explanation.en: A club has no owner to hold capital, so the members' collective stake is the accumulated fund.
explanation.ms: Kelab tiada pemilik yang memegang modal, jadi kepentingan bersama ahli ialah kumpulan wang terkumpul.

prompt.en: In a club, income exceeding expenditure is called a...
prompt.ms: Dalam kelab, pendapatan yang melebihi perbelanjaan dipanggil...

explanation.en: A club is not trading for profit, so the excess is a surplus — and a shortfall is a deficit.
explanation.ms: Kelab tidak berniaga untuk untung, jadi lebihannya ialah lebihan — dan kekurangan ialah defisit.

prompt.en: Subscriptions still owed by members at the year end are shown in the statement of financial position as...
prompt.ms: Yuran yang masih terhutang oleh ahli pada akhir tahun ditunjukkan dalam penyata kedudukan kewangan sebagai...

explanation.en: The club is owed money — arrears are accrued income, exactly like a receivable.
explanation.ms: Kelab dihutang wang — tunggakan ialah pendapatan terakru, sama seperti penghutang.

prompt.en: Subscriptions received in advance for next year are shown in the statement of financial position as...
prompt.ms: Yuran diterima terdahulu bagi tahun depan ditunjukkan dalam penyata kedudukan kewangan sebagai...

explanation.en: The club owes those members a year of membership it has not yet provided.
explanation.ms: Kelab berhutang kepada ahli itu satu tahun keahlian yang belum disediakan.

prompt.en: Subscriptions received during the year were RM9,000, and RM700 is still owed by members at the year end. There are no other adjustments. What is the subscription income for the year?
prompt.ms: Yuran diterima sepanjang tahun ialah RM9,000, dan RM700 masih terhutang oleh ahli pada akhir tahun. Tiada pelarasan lain. Berapakah pendapatan yuran bagi tahun itu?

explanation.en: 9,000 + 700 = 9,700. The club earned that RM700 this year even though it has not arrived — the same rule as accrued income.
explanation.ms: 9,000 + 700 = 9,700. Kelab memperoleh RM700 itu tahun ini walaupun ia belum sampai — peraturan yang sama seperti pendapatan terakru.

prompt.en: Subscriptions received RM12,000. Arrears at the start RM800, arrears at the end RM600, advance at the start RM400, advance at the end RM500. What is the subscription income for the year?
prompt.ms: Yuran diterima RM12,000. Tunggakan awal RM800, tunggakan akhir RM600, terdahulu awal RM400, terdahulu akhir RM500. Berapakah pendapatan yuran bagi tahun itu?

explanation.en: 12,000 − 800 + 600 + 400 − 500 = 11,700. Opening arrears were collected this year but earned last year; closing arrears were earned this year but not collected.
explanation.ms: 12,000 − 800 + 600 + 400 − 500 = 11,700. Tunggakan awal dikutip tahun ini tetapi diperoleh tahun lepas; tunggakan akhir diperoleh tahun ini tetapi belum dikutip.

prompt.en: Sort these into the Income and Expenditure Account, then work out the surplus.
prompt.ms: Asingkan ini ke dalam Akaun Pendapatan dan Perbelanjaan, kemudian kira lebihannya.

explanation.en: Income 13,700 − expenditure 8,700 = surplus 5,000. Depreciation belongs here even though no cash moved.
explanation.ms: Pendapatan 13,700 − perbelanjaan 8,700 = lebihan 5,000. Susut nilai tergolong di sini walaupun tiada tunai bergerak.

prompt.en: Subscriptions are the one club figure that is almost never just the cash. Start from the cash received, then ask of each adjustment: does this belong to THIS year? Opening arrears were earned last year, so take them off; closing arrears were earned this year, so add them on. Opening advances were paid for this year, so add them; closing advances belong to next year, so take them off.
prompt.ms: Yuran ialah satu-satunya angka kelab yang hampir tidak pernah sama dengan tunai. Mula daripada tunai diterima, kemudian tanya bagi setiap pelarasan: adakah ini milik tahun INI? Tunggakan awal diperoleh tahun lepas, jadi tolak; tunggakan akhir diperoleh tahun ini, jadi tambah. Terdahulu awal dibayar untuk tahun ini, jadi tambah; terdahulu akhir milik tahun depan, jadi tolak.

prompt.en: The adjustments are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Pelarasan sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: Subscriptions received RM12,000. Arrears at the start RM800, arrears at the end RM600, advance at the start RM400, advance at the end RM500.
scenario.ms: Yuran diterima RM12,000. Tunggakan awal RM800, tunggakan akhir RM600, terdahulu awal RM400, terdahulu akhir RM500.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Work out the subscription income.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Kira pendapatan yuran.

scenario.en: Subscriptions received RM15,000. Arrears at the start RM1,000, arrears at the end RM1,200, advance at the start RM300, advance at the end RM700.
scenario.ms: Yuran diterima RM15,000. Tunggakan awal RM1,000, tunggakan akhir RM1,200, terdahulu awal RM300, terdahulu akhir RM700.

explanation.en: 15,000 − 1,000 + 1,200 + 300 − 700 = 14,800. The two arrears lines pull opposite ways, and so do the two advance lines.
explanation.ms: 15,000 − 1,000 + 1,200 + 300 − 700 = 14,800. Dua baris tunggakan menarik arah bertentangan, begitu juga dua baris terdahulu.

prompt.en: Only the cash received is given. Work out the subscription income.
prompt.ms: Hanya tunai diterima diberi. Kira pendapatan yuran.

scenario.en: Subscriptions received RM20,000. Arrears at the start RM1,500, arrears at the end RM900, advance at the start RM600, advance at the end RM1,100.
scenario.ms: Yuran diterima RM20,000. Tunggakan awal RM1,500, tunggakan akhir RM900, terdahulu awal RM600, terdahulu akhir RM1,100.

explanation.en: 20,000 − 1,500 + 900 + 600 − 1,100 = 18,900. Here the income is LESS than the cash — a lot of last year's arrears were collected this year.
explanation.ms: 20,000 − 1,500 + 900 + 600 − 1,100 = 18,900. Di sini pendapatan KURANG daripada tunai — banyak tunggakan tahun lepas dikutip tahun ini.

prompt.en: With two or more owners, one capital account is no longer enough — you must be able to see what each partner is entitled to. So each partner gets TWO accounts. The CAPITAL account holds their permanent investment and barely moves. The CURRENT account holds everything that changes year to year: credited with their share of profit, interest on capital and any salary; debited with drawings and interest on drawings. Anything a partner earns from the business is a credit to their current account; anything they take out is a debit.
prompt.ms: Dengan dua atau lebih pemilik, satu akaun modal tidak lagi mencukupi — anda mesti dapat melihat hak setiap pekongsi. Jadi setiap pekongsi mendapat DUA akaun. Akaun MODAL memegang pelaburan tetap mereka dan jarang berubah. Akaun SEMASA memegang segala yang berubah dari tahun ke tahun: dikredit dengan bahagian untung, faedah atas modal dan sebarang gaji; didebit dengan ambilan dan faedah atas ambilan. Apa sahaja yang pekongsi peroleh daripada perniagaan ialah kredit ke akaun semasa; apa sahaja yang mereka ambil ialah debit.

prompt.en: A partner's share of the year's profit is credited to which account?
prompt.ms: Bahagian untung tahunan seorang pekongsi dikreditkan ke akaun yang mana?

explanation.en: Profit share changes every year, so it belongs in the current account — the capital account is for the permanent stake.
explanation.ms: Bahagian untung berubah setiap tahun, jadi ia masuk akaun semasa — akaun modal untuk pegangan tetap.

prompt.en: A partner pays in a further RM20,000 as a permanent investment. Which account is credited?
prompt.ms: Seorang pekongsi memasukkan RM20,000 lagi sebagai pelaburan tetap. Akaun manakah dikreditkan?

explanation.en: A permanent increase in what the partner has invested goes to the capital account.
explanation.ms: Pertambahan tetap dalam pelaburan pekongsi masuk ke akaun modal.

prompt.en: A partner's drawings during the year are debited to which account?
prompt.ms: Ambilan seorang pekongsi sepanjang tahun didebitkan ke akaun yang mana?

explanation.en: Drawings are part of the year-to-year movement, so they reduce the current account, not the capital.
explanation.ms: Ambilan sebahagian daripada pergerakan tahunan, jadi ia mengurangkan akaun semasa, bukan modal.

prompt.en: In a partner's current account, interest on capital is entered on the...
prompt.ms: Dalam akaun semasa pekongsi, faedah atas modal dicatat di sebelah...

explanation.en: The partner earns it for leaving money in the business, so it increases what the business owes them.
explanation.ms: Pekongsi memperolehnya kerana meninggalkan wang dalam perniagaan, jadi ia menambah hutang perniagaan kepada mereka.

prompt.en: In a partner's current account, interest on drawings is entered on the...
prompt.ms: Dalam akaun semasa pekongsi, faedah atas ambilan dicatat di sebelah...

explanation.en: It is a charge ON the partner for taking money out early — the opposite direction to interest on capital.
explanation.ms: Ia caj KE ATAS pekongsi kerana mengambil wang awal — arah bertentangan dengan faedah atas modal.

prompt.en: In the appropriation account, interest on drawings is...
prompt.ms: Dalam akaun pengagihan, faedah atas ambilan adalah...

explanation.en: The partners are charged it, so it comes back INTO the pool of profit available to share. It is the one line that goes up.
explanation.ms: Pekongsi dicaj untuknya, jadi ia kembali MASUK ke dalam untung yang boleh dibahagi. Ia satu-satunya baris yang naik.

prompt.en: In the appropriation account, a partner's salary is...
prompt.ms: Dalam akaun pengagihan, gaji seorang pekongsi adalah...

explanation.en: It is taken out before the rest is shared — a partner's salary is an appropriation of profit, never an expense in the income statement.
explanation.ms: Ia dikeluarkan sebelum yang selebihnya dibahagi — gaji pekongsi ialah pengagihan untung, bukan belanja dalam penyata pendapatan.

prompt.en: Net profit RM60,000. Interest on capital: Ali RM4,000, Bakar RM3,000. Salary to Bakar RM8,000. Interest on drawings: Ali RM500, Bakar RM300. What is the residual profit left to share?
prompt.ms: Untung bersih RM60,000. Faedah atas modal: Ali RM4,000, Bakar RM3,000. Gaji kepada Bakar RM8,000. Faedah atas ambilan: Ali RM500, Bakar RM300. Berapakah untung baki yang tinggal untuk dibahagi?

explanation.en: 60,000 − 4,000 − 3,000 − 8,000 + 800 = 45,800. Everything the partners are entitled to comes out first; the interest they are charged goes back in.
explanation.ms: 60,000 − 4,000 − 3,000 − 8,000 + 800 = 45,800. Semua hak pekongsi dikeluarkan dahulu; faedah yang dicaj kepada mereka dimasukkan semula.

prompt.en: Residual profit of RM45,800 is shared between Ali and Bakar in the ratio 3:2. What is Ali's share?
prompt.ms: Untung baki RM45,800 dibahagi antara Ali dan Bakar dengan nisbah 3:2. Berapakah bahagian Ali?

explanation.ms: 3 + 2 = 5 bahagian, jadi Ali mengambil 3/5: 45,800 × 3 ÷ 5 = 27,480.

prompt.en: Post these to Ali's Current Account, then find the closing balance.
prompt.ms: Catat ini ke Akaun Semasa Ali, kemudian cari baki penutup.

explanation.en: Credits 2,000 + 4,000 + 27,480 = 33,480. Debits 15,000 + 500 = 15,500. Balance 17,980 credit — the business still owes Ali that much.
explanation.ms: Kredit 2,000 + 4,000 + 27,480 = 33,480. Debit 15,000 + 500 = 15,500. Baki 17,980 kredit — perniagaan masih berhutang sebanyak itu kepada Ali.

prompt.en: The appropriation account always runs in the same order: start at net profit, take out everything the partners are individually entitled to (interest on capital, then salaries), add back the interest they are charged on drawings, and whatever remains is shared in the profit-sharing ratio. Only the last line of the first rung is blank; after that more of it goes.
prompt.ms: Akaun pengagihan sentiasa berjalan dalam susunan yang sama: mula pada untung bersih, keluarkan segala hak individu pekongsi (faedah atas modal, kemudian gaji), tambah semula faedah yang dicaj atas ambilan, dan apa yang tinggal dibahagi mengikut nisbah perkongsian untung. Hanya baris terakhir anak tangga pertama yang kosong; selepas itu lebih banyak hilang.

prompt.en: The appropriation is done. Work out Ali's share.
prompt.ms: Pengagihan sudah siap. Kira bahagian Ali.

scenario.en: Net profit RM60,000. Interest on capital: Ali RM4,000, Bakar RM3,000. Salary to Bakar RM8,000. Interest on drawings totals RM800. Ali and Bakar share profits 3:2.
scenario.ms: Untung bersih RM60,000. Faedah atas modal: Ali RM4,000, Bakar RM3,000. Gaji kepada Bakar RM8,000. Faedah atas ambilan berjumlah RM800. Ali dan Bakar berkongsi untung 3:2.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete the appropriation.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan pengagihan.

scenario.en: Net profit RM80,000. Interest on capital: Ali RM5,000, Bakar RM4,000. Salary to Bakar RM10,000. Interest on drawings totals RM1,000. Ali and Bakar share profits 3:2.
scenario.ms: Untung bersih RM80,000. Faedah atas modal: Ali RM5,000, Bakar RM4,000. Gaji kepada Bakar RM10,000. Faedah atas ambilan berjumlah RM1,000. Ali dan Bakar berkongsi untung 3:2.

explanation.en: 80,000 − 5,000 − 4,000 − 10,000 + 1,000 = 62,000, and 62,000 × 3 ÷ 5 = 37,200. Interest on drawings is the only line that is ADDED.
explanation.ms: 80,000 − 5,000 − 4,000 − 10,000 + 1,000 = 62,000, dan 62,000 × 3 ÷ 5 = 37,200. Faedah atas ambilan satu-satunya baris yang DITAMBAH.

prompt.en: Only the net profit is given. Work the whole appropriation.
prompt.ms: Hanya untung bersih diberi. Kerjakan keseluruhan pengagihan.

scenario.en: Net profit RM50,000. Interest on capital: Ali RM3,000, Bakar RM2,000. Salary to Bakar RM6,000. Interest on drawings totals RM500. Ali and Bakar share profits 3:2.
scenario.ms: Untung bersih RM50,000. Faedah atas modal: Ali RM3,000, Bakar RM2,000. Gaji kepada Bakar RM6,000. Faedah atas ambilan berjumlah RM500. Ali dan Bakar berkongsi untung 3:2.

explanation.en: 50,000 − 3,000 − 2,000 − 6,000 + 500 = 39,500, and 39,500 × 3 ÷ 5 = 23,700. Bakar takes the other 2/5 — RM15,800 — plus his salary and interest on capital.
explanation.ms: 50,000 − 3,000 − 2,000 − 6,000 + 500 = 39,500, dan 39,500 × 3 ÷ 5 = 23,700. Bakar mengambil 2/5 yang lain — RM15,800 — campur gaji dan faedah atas modalnya.

prompt.en: A company is owned by its shareholders and financed partly by lenders. Share capital and every reserve belong to the owners, so they are equity. A debenture is a loan: the holder is a lender, not an owner, and must be paid interest whether or not the company makes a profit.
prompt.ms: Syarikat dimiliki oleh pemegang sahamnya dan sebahagian pembiayaannya datang daripada pemberi pinjaman. Modal saham dan setiap rizab adalah milik pemilik, jadi ia ekuiti. Debentur pula ialah pinjaman: pemegangnya pemberi pinjaman, bukan pemilik, dan mesti dibayar faedah sama ada syarikat untung atau tidak.

prompt.en: Where does Ordinary Share Capital belong?
prompt.ms: Di manakah Modal Saham Biasa tergolong?

explanation.en: Ordinary shareholders own the company, so what they put in is equity.
explanation.ms: Pemegang saham biasa memiliki syarikat, jadi apa yang mereka masukkan ialah ekuiti.

prompt.en: Where do 8% Debentures repayable in 2035 belong?
prompt.ms: Di manakah Debentur 8% yang perlu dibayar balik pada 2035 tergolong?

explanation.en: A debenture is a long-term loan, not ownership. It is repayable more than a year away, so it is a non-current liability — and its interest is an expense, not a dividend.
explanation.ms: Debentur ialah pinjaman jangka panjang, bukan pemilikan. Ia perlu dibayar balik lebih setahun lagi, jadi ia liabiliti bukan semasa — dan faedahnya ialah belanja, bukan dividen.

prompt.en: Where does Retained Profit belong?
prompt.ms: Di manakah Untung Tertahan tergolong?

explanation.en: Retained profit is profit the owners have earned but left in the business, so it is still theirs.
explanation.ms: Untung tertahan ialah untung yang telah diperoleh pemilik tetapi dibiarkan dalam perniagaan, jadi ia masih milik mereka.

prompt.en: Where does a Proposed Ordinary Dividend belong?
prompt.ms: Di manakah Dividen Biasa Dicadangkan tergolong?

explanation.en: Once a dividend is proposed the company owes it to the shareholders and will pay it within the year — an amount owed, not an amount held.
explanation.ms: Sebaik dividen dicadangkan, syarikat terhutang kepada pemegang saham dan akan membayarnya dalam tahun ini — jumlah yang terhutang, bukan yang dipegang.

prompt.en: Where does a General Reserve belong?
prompt.ms: Di manakah Rizab Am tergolong?

explanation.en: Transferring profit to a general reserve moves it from one equity pocket to another. Nothing leaves the company, so it never becomes a liability.
explanation.ms: Memindahkan untung ke rizab am hanya mengalihkannya dari satu poket ekuiti ke poket ekuiti yang lain. Tiada apa yang keluar dari syarikat, jadi ia tidak pernah menjadi liabiliti.

prompt.en: The company pays its debenture interest by cheque. The Debenture Interest account is...
prompt.ms: Syarikat membayar faedah debenturnya dengan cek. Akaun Faedah Debentur ialah...

explanation.en: Debenture interest is an expense, and an expense increasing is debited. The credit goes to Bank.
explanation.ms: Faedah debentur ialah belanja, dan belanja yang bertambah didebitkan. Kreditnya pula ke akaun Bank.

prompt.en: Once profit after tax is known, the company decides what to do with it: park some in a reserve, pay the preference shareholders their fixed percentage, pay the ordinary shareholders whatever is declared, and carry the rest forward. Interest is NOT part of this — it was already deducted to arrive at the profit.
prompt.ms: Setelah untung selepas cukai diketahui, syarikat memutuskan apa yang hendak dibuat dengannya: menyimpan sebahagian dalam rizab, membayar pemegang saham keutamaan peratusan tetap mereka, membayar pemegang saham biasa apa yang diisytiharkan, dan membawa bakinya ke hadapan. Faedah BUKAN sebahagian daripada ini — ia sudah ditolak sebelum untung diperoleh.

prompt.en: A company has 200,000 6% preference shares of RM1 each. How much is the preference dividend for the year?
prompt.ms: Sebuah syarikat mempunyai 200,000 saham keutamaan 6% bernilai RM1 setiap satu. Berapakah dividen keutamaan bagi tahun tersebut?

explanation.en: 6% of RM200,000 = RM12,000. A preference dividend is a fixed percentage of the preference share capital — it does not change with profit.
explanation.ms: 6% daripada RM200,000 = RM12,000. Dividen keutamaan ialah peratusan tetap daripada modal saham keutamaan — ia tidak berubah mengikut untung.

prompt.en: A company declares an ordinary dividend of 4 sen per share on 500,000 ordinary shares. How much is the ordinary dividend?
prompt.ms: Sebuah syarikat mengisytiharkan dividen biasa 4 sen sesaham ke atas 500,000 saham biasa. Berapakah dividen biasa itu?

explanation.en: 500,000 × RM0.04 = RM20,000. An ordinary dividend is declared per SHARE, so it depends on the number of shares, not on their value.
explanation.ms: 500,000 × RM0.04 = RM20,000. Dividen biasa diisytiharkan bagi setiap SAHAM, jadi ia bergantung pada bilangan saham, bukan pada nilainya.

prompt.en: Profit after tax RM150,000. Transfer to general reserve RM25,000, preference dividend RM12,000, ordinary dividend RM20,000. What is the retained profit for the year?
prompt.ms: Untung selepas cukai RM150,000. Pindahan ke rizab am RM25,000, dividen keutamaan RM12,000, dividen biasa RM20,000. Berapakah untung tertahan bagi tahun tersebut?

explanation.en: 150,000 − 25,000 − 12,000 − 20,000 = 93,000. All three are appropriations of profit already earned.
explanation.ms: 150,000 − 25,000 − 12,000 − 20,000 = 93,000. Ketiga-tiganya ialah pengagihan untung yang telah diperoleh.

prompt.en: Retained profit brought forward is RM60,000 and the retained profit for the year is RM93,000. What is the retained profit carried forward?
prompt.ms: Untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan ialah RM60,000 dan untung tertahan bagi tahun ini RM93,000. Berapakah untung tertahan yang dibawa ke hadapan?

explanation.en: 60,000 + 93,000 = 153,000. Retained profit accumulates year after year — it is a running total, not a single year's figure.
explanation.ms: 60,000 + 93,000 = 153,000. Untung tertahan terkumpul dari tahun ke tahun — ia jumlah berjalan, bukan angka satu tahun sahaja.

prompt.en: Debenture interest is...
prompt.ms: Faedah debentur ialah...

options: An expense in the income statement

items.answer: An expense in the income statement

explanation.en: This is the classic trap. Interest is the cost of borrowing and is deducted BEFORE profit is arrived at; a dividend is a share of profit already earned. Treating interest as an appropriation overstates the profit.
explanation.ms: Inilah perangkap klasiknya. Faedah ialah kos meminjam dan ditolak SEBELUM untung diperoleh; dividen pula ialah bahagian daripada untung yang sudah diperoleh. Menganggap faedah sebagai pengagihan akan melebihkan untung.

prompt.en: The appropriation runs top to bottom in one direction: start from profit after tax, take off every appropriation, and what is left joins the retained profit already carried forward from last year. Each rung below hands you less of it.
prompt.ms: Pengagihan berjalan dari atas ke bawah dalam satu arah: mula dari untung selepas cukai, tolak setiap pengagihan, dan apa yang tinggal bergabung dengan untung tertahan yang sudah dibawa ke hadapan dari tahun lepas. Setiap anak tangga di bawah memberi anda kurang daripadanya.

prompt.en: The workings are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Kerja kira sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: Profit after tax RM150,000. Transfer to general reserve RM25,000. Preference dividend RM12,000. Ordinary dividend RM20,000. Retained profit brought forward RM60,000.
scenario.ms: Untung selepas cukai RM150,000. Pindahan ke rizab am RM25,000. Dividen keutamaan RM12,000. Dividen biasa RM20,000. Untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan RM60,000.

label.ms: Tambah: untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan

explanation.en: 93,000 + 60,000 = 153,000. The carried-forward figure is what appears in the equity section of the statement of financial position.
explanation.ms: 93,000 + 60,000 = 153,000. Angka yang dibawa ke hadapan inilah yang muncul dalam bahagian ekuiti penyata kedudukan kewangan.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete the appropriation.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan pengagihan itu.

scenario.en: Profit after tax RM210,000. Transfer to general reserve RM40,000. Preference dividend RM9,000. Ordinary dividend RM36,000. Retained profit brought forward RM85,000.
scenario.ms: Untung selepas cukai RM210,000. Pindahan ke rizab am RM40,000. Dividen keutamaan RM9,000. Dividen biasa RM36,000. Untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan RM85,000.

label.ms: Tambah: untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan

explanation.en: 210,000 − 40,000 − 9,000 − 36,000 = 125,000, plus 85,000 brought forward = 210,000. Notice the year's profit and the closing retained profit are equal here purely by coincidence — they measure different things.
explanation.ms: 210,000 − 40,000 − 9,000 − 36,000 = 125,000, tambah 85,000 dibawa ke hadapan = 210,000. Perhatikan untung tahun ini dan untung tertahan penutup adalah sama di sini secara kebetulan sahaja — kedua-duanya mengukur perkara berbeza.

prompt.en: Only the profit after tax is given. Build the whole appropriation.
prompt.ms: Hanya untung selepas cukai diberi. Bina keseluruhan pengagihan.

scenario.en: Profit after tax RM96,000. Transfer to general reserve RM15,000. Preference dividend RM6,000. Ordinary dividend RM25,000. Retained profit brought forward RM42,000.
scenario.ms: Untung selepas cukai RM96,000. Pindahan ke rizab am RM15,000. Dividen keutamaan RM6,000. Dividen biasa RM25,000. Untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan RM42,000.

label.ms: Tambah: untung tertahan dibawa ke hadapan

explanation.en: 96,000 − 15,000 − 6,000 − 25,000 = 50,000, plus 42,000 = 92,000. Every line after the first reduces the profit except the last two, which add back what was already there.
explanation.ms: 96,000 − 15,000 − 6,000 − 25,000 = 50,000, tambah 42,000 = 92,000. Setiap baris selepas yang pertama mengurangkan untung kecuali dua baris terakhir, yang menambah semula apa yang sudah ada.

title.ms: Langsung, Tak Langsung atau Bukan Kilang

prompt.en: A cost is DIRECT if you can trace it to the product itself — the material in it, the wages of the person who made it, a royalty paid on each unit. A cost is a factory OVERHEAD if it keeps the factory running but cannot be traced to one unit. A cost that has nothing to do with the factory never enters the manufacturing account at all.
prompt.ms: Sesuatu kos adalah LANGSUNG jika ia boleh dikesan terus kepada produk itu sendiri — bahan di dalamnya, gaji orang yang membuatnya, royalti yang dibayar bagi setiap unit. Sesuatu kos ialah OVERHED kilang jika ia mengekalkan operasi kilang tetapi tidak boleh dikesan kepada satu unit. Kos yang tiada kaitan dengan kilang langsung tidak masuk ke dalam akaun pengilangan.

prompt.en: Raw materials bought for production are...
prompt.ms: Bahan mentah yang dibeli untuk pengeluaran ialah...

explanation.en: The material physically becomes part of the finished product, so it is traceable to it.
explanation.ms: Bahan itu secara fizikal menjadi sebahagian daripada produk siap, jadi ia boleh dikesan kepadanya.

prompt.en: The wages of the machine operators who make the product are...
prompt.ms: Gaji pengendali mesin yang membuat produk itu ialah...

explanation.en: They work on the product itself, so their wages are traceable to it.
explanation.ms: Mereka bekerja pada produk itu sendiri, jadi gaji mereka boleh dikesan kepadanya.

prompt.en: The salary of the factory supervisor is...
prompt.ms: Gaji penyelia kilang ialah...

explanation.en: The supervisor is in the factory but does not work on any one product, so the cost cannot be traced to a unit — indirect, not direct labour.
explanation.ms: Penyelia berada di kilang tetapi tidak bekerja pada mana-mana produk tertentu, jadi kosnya tidak boleh dikesan kepada satu unit — tak langsung, bukan buruh langsung.

prompt.en: Depreciation of factory machinery is...
prompt.ms: Susut nilai jentera kilang ialah...

explanation.en: It is a cost of running the factory, spread across everything made there. Depreciation of OFFICE equipment would not belong here at all.
explanation.ms: Ia kos mengendalikan kilang, tersebar merentasi segala yang dibuat di situ. Susut nilai peralatan PEJABAT pula langsung tidak tergolong di sini.

prompt.en: A royalty paid to a designer on every unit produced is...
prompt.ms: Royalti yang dibayar kepada pereka bagi setiap unit yang dikeluarkan ialah...

explanation.en: It rises and falls exactly with output and is traceable to each unit, but it is neither material nor labour — that is what a direct expense is. It belongs in prime cost.
explanation.ms: Ia naik dan turun tepat mengikut pengeluaran dan boleh dikesan kepada setiap unit, tetapi ia bukan bahan mahupun buruh — itulah maksud belanja langsung. Ia tergolong dalam kos prima.

prompt.en: Office stationery is...
prompt.ms: Alat tulis pejabat ialah...

explanation.en: Nothing about it touches production. It is an expense of the income statement and never enters the manufacturing account.
explanation.ms: Tiada apa padanya yang menyentuh pengeluaran. Ia belanja penyata pendapatan dan tidak pernah masuk ke akaun pengilangan.

prompt.en: The manufacturing account is built in a fixed order: work out the materials actually used, add the direct costs to get prime cost, add the factory overheads, adjust for work still unfinished at each end, and you have the cost of production. Only then does the income statement take over.
prompt.ms: Akaun pengilangan dibina mengikut susunan tetap: kira bahan yang benar-benar digunakan, tambah kos langsung untuk mendapat kos prima, tambah overhed kilang, laraskan untuk kerja yang belum siap di kedua-dua hujung, dan anda akan dapat kos pengeluaran. Barulah penyata pendapatan mengambil alih.

prompt.en: Opening raw materials RM8,000. Purchases of raw materials RM52,000. Carriage inwards RM2,000. Closing raw materials RM6,000. What is the cost of raw materials consumed?
prompt.ms: Bahan mentah awal RM8,000. Belian bahan mentah RM52,000. Angkutan masuk RM2,000. Bahan mentah akhir RM6,000. Berapakah kos bahan mentah yang digunakan?

explanation.en: 8,000 + 52,000 + 2,000 − 6,000 = 56,000. Carriage inwards is part of the cost of getting the material in, so it is added to purchases — never treated as an overhead.
explanation.ms: 8,000 + 52,000 + 2,000 − 6,000 = 56,000. Angkutan masuk ialah sebahagian daripada kos membawa masuk bahan, jadi ia ditambah kepada belian — bukan dianggap overhed.

prompt.en: Raw materials consumed RM56,000. Direct wages RM34,000. Royalties on units produced RM3,000. What is the prime cost?
prompt.ms: Bahan mentah digunakan RM56,000. Upah langsung RM34,000. Royalti atas unit dikeluarkan RM3,000. Berapakah kos prima?

explanation.en: 56,000 + 34,000 + 3,000 = 93,000. Prime cost is every DIRECT cost added together — material, labour and direct expense — and nothing else.
explanation.ms: 56,000 + 34,000 + 3,000 = 93,000. Kos prima ialah setiap kos LANGSUNG yang dijumlahkan — bahan, buruh dan belanja langsung — dan tiada yang lain.

prompt.en: Factory rent RM12,000. Indirect wages RM9,000. Depreciation of factory machinery RM5,000. What are the total factory overheads?
prompt.ms: Sewa kilang RM12,000. Upah tak langsung RM9,000. Susut nilai jentera kilang RM5,000. Berapakah jumlah overhed kilang?

explanation.en: 12,000 + 9,000 + 5,000 = 26,000. Every one of these keeps the factory running without being traceable to a single unit.
explanation.ms: 12,000 + 9,000 + 5,000 = 26,000. Setiap satu daripadanya mengekalkan operasi kilang tanpa boleh dikesan kepada satu unit.

prompt.en: Prime cost RM93,000. Factory overheads RM26,000. Opening work in progress RM4,000. Closing work in progress RM7,000. What is the cost of production?
prompt.ms: Kos prima RM93,000. Overhed kilang RM26,000. Kerja dalam proses awal RM4,000. Kerja dalam proses akhir RM7,000. Berapakah kos pengeluaran?

explanation.en: 93,000 + 26,000 + 4,000 − 7,000 = 116,000. Opening work in progress is finished this year so it is added; closing work in progress is not finished yet, so it is taken out.
explanation.ms: 93,000 + 26,000 + 4,000 − 7,000 = 116,000. Kerja dalam proses awal disiapkan tahun ini jadi ia ditambah; kerja dalam proses akhir belum siap, jadi ia dikeluarkan.

prompt.en: Opening finished goods RM15,000. Cost of production RM116,000. Closing finished goods RM11,000. What is the cost of sales?
prompt.ms: Barang siap awal RM15,000. Kos pengeluaran RM116,000. Barang siap akhir RM11,000. Berapakah kos jualan?

explanation.en: 15,000 + 116,000 − 11,000 = 120,000. In a manufacturing business the cost of production replaces purchases in the cost of sales working.
explanation.ms: 15,000 + 116,000 − 11,000 = 120,000. Dalam perniagaan pengilangan, kos pengeluaran menggantikan belian dalam kerja kira kos jualan.

prompt.en: The manufacturing account never changes shape: direct costs give prime cost, overheads are added on top, then the two work-in-progress figures adjust for what was unfinished at each end. Each rung below takes one more line away.
prompt.ms: Akaun pengilangan tidak pernah berubah bentuk: kos langsung memberi kos prima, overhed ditambah di atasnya, kemudian dua angka kerja dalam proses melaraskan apa yang belum siap di kedua-dua hujung. Setiap anak tangga di bawah menanggalkan satu baris lagi.

prompt.en: The workings are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Kerja kira sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: Raw materials consumed RM56,000. Direct wages RM34,000. Factory overheads RM26,000. Opening work in progress RM4,000. Closing work in progress RM7,000.
scenario.ms: Bahan mentah digunakan RM56,000. Upah langsung RM34,000. Overhed kilang RM26,000. Kerja dalam proses awal RM4,000. Kerja dalam proses akhir RM7,000.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete the manufacturing account.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan akaun pengilangan.

scenario.en: Raw materials consumed RM72,000. Direct wages RM41,000. Factory overheads RM30,000. Opening work in progress RM6,000. Closing work in progress RM9,000.
scenario.ms: Bahan mentah digunakan RM72,000. Upah langsung RM41,000. Overhed kilang RM30,000. Kerja dalam proses awal RM6,000. Kerja dalam proses akhir RM9,000.

explanation.en: 72,000 + 41,000 = 113,000 prime cost, then + 30,000 + 6,000 − 9,000 = 140,000. Overheads are added AFTER prime cost, never inside it.
explanation.ms: 72,000 + 41,000 = 113,000 kos prima, kemudian + 30,000 + 6,000 − 9,000 = 140,000. Overhed ditambah SELEPAS kos prima, bukan di dalamnya.

prompt.en: Only the materials figure is given. Build the whole manufacturing account.
prompt.ms: Hanya angka bahan diberi. Bina keseluruhan akaun pengilangan.

scenario.en: Raw materials consumed RM48,000. Direct wages RM27,000. Factory overheads RM22,000. Opening work in progress RM5,000. Closing work in progress RM3,000.
scenario.ms: Bahan mentah digunakan RM48,000. Upah langsung RM27,000. Overhed kilang RM22,000. Kerja dalam proses awal RM5,000. Kerja dalam proses akhir RM3,000.

explanation.en: 48,000 + 27,000 = 75,000, + 22,000 + 5,000 − 3,000 = 99,000. Here closing work in progress is smaller than opening, so the adjustment adds to the cost overall — the direction follows the figures, not a rule to memorise.
explanation.ms: 48,000 + 27,000 = 75,000, + 22,000 + 5,000 − 3,000 = 99,000. Di sini kerja dalam proses akhir lebih kecil daripada yang awal, jadi pelarasan itu menambah kos secara keseluruhan — arahnya mengikut angka, bukan peraturan untuk dihafal.

prompt.en: A ratio compares two figures that already exist in the statements. Get the two figures the right way round and the arithmetic is easy: margin is measured against SALES, mark-up against COST, and a liquidity ratio compares what you can turn into cash against what you owe soon.
prompt.ms: Nisbah membandingkan dua angka yang sudah wujud dalam penyata. Dapatkan kedua-dua angka dalam susunan yang betul dan pengiraannya mudah: margin diukur terhadap JUALAN, tokokan terhadap KOS, dan nisbah kecairan membandingkan apa yang boleh ditukar kepada tunai dengan apa yang perlu dibayar tidak lama lagi.

prompt.en: Sales RM500,000 and gross profit RM100,000. What is the gross profit margin?
prompt.ms: Jualan RM500,000 dan untung kasar RM100,000. Berapakah margin untung kasar?

explanation.en: 100,000 ÷ 500,000 × 100 = 20%. A MARGIN is always measured against sales.
explanation.ms: 100,000 ÷ 500,000 × 100 = 20%. MARGIN sentiasa diukur terhadap jualan.

prompt.en: Same business: gross profit RM100,000 and cost of sales RM400,000. What is the mark-up?
prompt.ms: Perniagaan yang sama: untung kasar RM100,000 dan kos jualan RM400,000. Berapakah tokokan?

explanation.en: 100,000 ÷ 400,000 × 100 = 25%. Same profit, different base: a 20% margin is a 25% mark-up. Dividing by the wrong figure is the most common error in this whole topic.
explanation.ms: 100,000 ÷ 400,000 × 100 = 25%. Untung yang sama, asas yang berbeza: margin 20% ialah tokokan 25%. Membahagi dengan angka yang salah ialah kesilapan paling lazim dalam keseluruhan topik ini.

prompt.en: Sales RM500,000 and net profit RM60,000. What is the net profit margin?
prompt.ms: Jualan RM500,000 dan untung bersih RM60,000. Berapakah margin untung bersih?

explanation.en: 60,000 ÷ 500,000 × 100 = 12%. The gap between this and the gross margin is what the expenses cost the business.
explanation.ms: 60,000 ÷ 500,000 × 100 = 12%. Jurang antara ini dan margin kasar ialah kos belanja kepada perniagaan.

prompt.en: Current assets RM150,000 and current liabilities RM50,000. What is the current ratio?
prompt.ms: Aset semasa RM150,000 dan liabiliti semasa RM50,000. Berapakah nisbah semasa?

explanation.en: 150,000 ÷ 50,000 = 3. The business has RM3 of short-term assets for every RM1 it owes soon.
explanation.ms: 150,000 ÷ 50,000 = 3. Perniagaan mempunyai RM3 aset jangka pendek bagi setiap RM1 yang perlu dibayar tidak lama lagi.

prompt.en: Current assets RM150,000, of which inventory is RM50,000. Current liabilities RM50,000. What is the acid test ratio?
prompt.ms: Aset semasa RM150,000, termasuk inventori RM50,000. Liabiliti semasa RM50,000. Berapakah nisbah ujian asid?

explanation.en: (150,000 − 50,000) ÷ 50,000 = 2. Inventory is removed because it still has to be SOLD before it becomes cash — that is the whole point of the acid test.
explanation.ms: (150,000 − 50,000) ÷ 50,000 = 2. Inventori dikeluarkan kerana ia masih perlu DIJUAL sebelum menjadi tunai — itulah tujuan ujian asid.

prompt.en: Net profit RM60,000 and capital employed RM400,000. What is the return on capital employed?
prompt.ms: Untung bersih RM60,000 dan modal diguna RM400,000. Berapakah pulangan atas modal diguna?

explanation.en: 60,000 ÷ 400,000 × 100 = 15%. This is the ratio an owner compares against simply leaving the money in the bank.
explanation.ms: 60,000 ÷ 400,000 × 100 = 15%. Inilah nisbah yang dibandingkan oleh pemilik dengan sekadar meninggalkan wangnya di bank.

prompt.en: A ratio on its own says nothing. It only means something next to last year's figure, or next to another business. What matters in an exam is being able to say WHICH figure must have moved to produce the change you can see.
prompt.ms: Nisbah dengan sendirinya tidak bermakna apa-apa. Ia hanya bermakna apabila diletakkan di sebelah angka tahun lepas, atau di sebelah perniagaan lain. Apa yang penting dalam peperiksaan ialah keupayaan menyatakan angka MANA yang mesti telah berubah sehingga menghasilkan perubahan yang anda lihat.

prompt.en: Cost of sales RM400,000 and average inventory RM50,000. What is the rate of inventory turnover?
prompt.ms: Kos jualan RM400,000 dan inventori purata RM50,000. Berapakah kadar pusing ganti inventori?

explanation.en: 400,000 ÷ 50,000 = 8 times. The business sells and replaces its whole inventory eight times a year — a higher figure usually means goods are not sitting on the shelf.
explanation.ms: 400,000 ÷ 50,000 = 8 kali. Perniagaan menjual dan menggantikan keseluruhan inventorinya lapan kali setahun — angka yang lebih tinggi biasanya bermakna barang tidak tersadai di rak.

prompt.en: Trade receivables RM30,000 and credit sales RM365,000. What is the debtors collection period, in days?
prompt.ms: Penghutang perdagangan RM30,000 dan jualan kredit RM365,000. Berapakah tempoh kutipan penghutang, dalam hari?

explanation.en: 30,000 ÷ 365,000 × 365 = 30 days. Only CREDIT sales are used — a cash sale was never owed in the first place.
explanation.ms: 30,000 ÷ 365,000 × 365 = 30 hari. Hanya jualan KREDIT digunakan — jualan tunai tidak pernah terhutang sejak awal lagi.

prompt.en: A shop's gross profit margin fell from 25% to 18% while its selling prices were unchanged. What must have happened?
prompt.ms: Margin untung kasar sebuah kedai jatuh dari 25% kepada 18% sedangkan harga jualannya tidak berubah. Apakah yang mesti telah berlaku?

explanation.en: Gross profit is sales minus cost of sales, so only those two can move it. Operating expenses come further down and change the NET margin, not the gross one. Falling sales alone would not change the percentage.
explanation.ms: Untung kasar ialah jualan tolak kos jualan, jadi hanya kedua-dua itu boleh mengubahnya. Belanja pengendalian datang lebih ke bawah dan mengubah margin BERSIH, bukan yang kasar. Jualan yang menurun sahaja tidak akan mengubah peratusannya.

prompt.en: A business has a current ratio of 0.8:1. What does this suggest?
prompt.ms: Sebuah perniagaan mempunyai nisbah semasa 0.8:1. Apakah yang ditunjukkan oleh ini?

options: It may not be able to pay its short-term debts
It is holding too much inventory
options_ms: Ia mungkin tidak mampu membayar hutang jangka pendeknya

items.answer: It may not be able to pay its short-term debts

explanation.en: Below 1:1 the current liabilities are larger than everything the business could turn into cash within the year.
explanation.ms: Di bawah 1:1, liabiliti semasa lebih besar daripada segala yang boleh ditukar oleh perniagaan kepada tunai dalam tahun itu.

prompt.en: A firm's debtors collection period rose from 30 days to 60 days. What does this mean?
prompt.ms: Tempoh kutipan penghutang sebuah firma meningkat dari 30 hari kepada 60 hari. Apakah maksudnya?

explanation.en: A LONGER period means the money sits with the customer for longer — worse for cash flow, even though sales themselves may look healthy.
explanation.ms: Tempoh yang LEBIH PANJANG bermakna wang berada lebih lama dengan pelanggan — lebih buruk untuk aliran tunai, walaupun jualan itu sendiri mungkin kelihatan sihat.

prompt.en: Both margins come out of the same short column: sales, minus cost of sales, gives gross profit and the gross margin; minus expenses gives net profit and the net margin. Every percentage on that column is measured against SALES. Each rung below hands you less of it.
prompt.ms: Kedua-dua margin terhasil daripada lajur pendek yang sama: jualan, tolak kos jualan, memberi untung kasar dan margin kasar; tolak belanja pula memberi untung bersih dan margin bersih. Setiap peratusan dalam lajur itu diukur terhadap JUALAN. Setiap anak tangga di bawah memberi anda kurang daripadanya.

prompt.en: The workings are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Kerja kira sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: Sales RM500,000. Cost of sales RM400,000. Expenses RM40,000. Give each margin in whole percent.
scenario.ms: Jualan RM500,000. Kos jualan RM400,000. Belanja RM40,000. Berikan setiap margin dalam peratus bulat.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete both margins.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan kedua-dua margin.

scenario.en: Sales RM250,000. Cost of sales RM175,000. Expenses RM25,000. Give each margin in whole percent.
scenario.ms: Jualan RM250,000. Kos jualan RM175,000. Belanja RM25,000. Berikan setiap margin dalam peratus bulat.

explanation.en: Gross profit 75,000 is 30% of sales; after 25,000 of expenses the net profit of 50,000 is 20% of sales. Both percentages use SALES as the base, never the profit above them.
explanation.ms: Untung kasar 75,000 ialah 30% daripada jualan; selepas belanja 25,000, untung bersih 50,000 ialah 20% daripada jualan. Kedua-dua peratusan menggunakan JUALAN sebagai asas, bukan untung di atasnya.

prompt.en: Only sales is given. Work out both margins from the scenario.
prompt.ms: Hanya jualan diberi. Kira kedua-dua margin daripada senario.

scenario.en: Sales RM800,000. Cost of sales RM600,000. Expenses RM120,000. Give each margin in whole percent.
scenario.ms: Jualan RM800,000. Kos jualan RM600,000. Belanja RM120,000. Berikan setiap margin dalam peratus bulat.

explanation.en: 800,000 − 600,000 = 200,000, which is 25% of sales; less 120,000 of expenses leaves 80,000, which is 10%. A wide gap between the two margins is a business whose expenses, not whose buying, are the problem.
explanation.ms: 800,000 − 600,000 = 200,000, iaitu 25% daripada jualan; tolak belanja 120,000 meninggalkan 80,000, iaitu 10%. Jurang lebar antara kedua-dua margin menunjukkan perniagaan yang masalahnya pada belanja, bukan pada pembelian.

prompt.en: A cash budget records MONEY moving, and nothing else. If cash comes in it is a receipt, if cash goes out it is a payment — and if no money changes hands at all, it does not appear, however large the figure is in the income statement.
prompt.ms: Belanjawan tunai merekod WANG yang bergerak, dan tiada yang lain. Jika tunai masuk ia terimaan, jika tunai keluar ia bayaran — dan jika tiada wang bertukar tangan langsung, ia tidak muncul, walau sebesar mana pun angkanya dalam penyata pendapatan.

prompt.en: Cash sales for the month are...
prompt.ms: Jualan tunai bagi bulan itu ialah...

explanation.en: Money comes in during the month it is sold, so it is a receipt of that month.
explanation.ms: Wang masuk dalam bulan ia dijual, jadi ia terimaan bulan itu.

prompt.en: A cheque paid to a supplier is...
prompt.ms: Cek yang dibayar kepada pembekal ialah...

explanation.en: Money leaves the bank, so it is a payment in the month the cheque is paid.
explanation.ms: Wang keluar dari bank, jadi ia bayaran dalam bulan cek itu dibayar.

prompt.en: Depreciation of the delivery van is...
prompt.ms: Susut nilai van penghantaran ialah...

explanation.en: Depreciation is an accounting charge, not a payment — no money leaves the business. The van was paid for once, when it was bought.
explanation.ms: Susut nilai ialah caj perakaunan, bukan bayaran — tiada wang keluar dari perniagaan. Van itu dibayar sekali sahaja, iaitu semasa ia dibeli.

prompt.en: A bad debt written off is...
prompt.ms: Hutang lapuk yang dihapus kira ialah...

explanation.en: Nothing is paid out — what happens is that a receipt you were expecting never arrives. It reduces the receipts you budget for, but it is not itself a payment.
explanation.ms: Tiada apa yang dibayar keluar — apa yang berlaku ialah terimaan yang anda jangkakan tidak pernah sampai. Ia mengurangkan terimaan yang dibelanjawankan, tetapi ia sendiri bukan bayaran.

prompt.en: A bank loan received is...
prompt.ms: Pinjaman bank yang diterima ialah...

explanation.en: Cash comes in, so it is a receipt — even though it is not income and never appears in the income statement.
explanation.ms: Tunai masuk, jadi ia terimaan — walaupun ia bukan pendapatan dan tidak pernah muncul dalam penyata pendapatan.

prompt.en: The owner's cash drawings are...
prompt.ms: Ambilan tunai pemilik ialah...

explanation.en: Cash leaves the business, so the budget must show it — again, even though drawings are not an expense.
explanation.ms: Tunai keluar dari perniagaan, jadi belanjawan mesti menunjukkannya — sekali lagi, walaupun ambilan bukan belanja.

prompt.en: The hard part of a cash budget is TIMING, not arithmetic. A credit sale is income in the month of sale but a receipt in the month the customer actually pays. Each month then runs the same three lines: opening balance, plus receipts, less payments — and the closing balance becomes next month's opening balance.
prompt.ms: Bahagian sukar belanjawan tunai ialah MASA, bukan pengiraan. Jualan kredit ialah pendapatan dalam bulan jualan tetapi terimaan dalam bulan pelanggan benar-benar membayar. Setiap bulan kemudiannya berjalan dengan tiga baris yang sama: baki awal, campur terimaan, tolak bayaran — dan baki akhir menjadi baki awal bulan berikutnya.

prompt.en: Customers pay one month after the sale. Credit sales were January RM20,000, February RM24,000, March RM30,000. How much is received from debtors in March?
prompt.ms: Pelanggan membayar sebulan selepas jualan. Jualan kredit ialah Januari RM20,000, Februari RM24,000, Mac RM30,000. Berapakah yang diterima daripada penghutang pada bulan Mac?

explanation.en: March's receipts are February's sales: RM24,000. March's own sales of RM30,000 will not be received until April.
explanation.ms: Terimaan Mac ialah jualan Februari: RM24,000. Jualan Mac sendiri sebanyak RM30,000 tidak akan diterima sehingga April.

prompt.en: In March, cash sales are RM12,000 and receipts from debtors are RM24,000. What are the total receipts for March?
prompt.ms: Pada bulan Mac, jualan tunai ialah RM12,000 dan terimaan daripada penghutang RM24,000. Berapakah jumlah terimaan bagi bulan Mac?

prompt.en: In March the business pays suppliers RM18,000, wages RM7,000 and rent RM3,000. What are the total payments for March?
prompt.ms: Pada bulan Mac perniagaan membayar pembekal RM18,000, gaji RM7,000 dan sewa RM3,000. Berapakah jumlah bayaran bagi bulan Mac?

prompt.en: March opens with RM5,000 in the bank. Receipts are RM36,000 and payments RM28,000. What is the closing balance at the end of March?
prompt.ms: Bulan Mac bermula dengan RM5,000 dalam bank. Terimaan RM36,000 dan bayaran RM28,000. Berapakah baki akhir pada penghujung Mac?

prompt.en: April opens with March's closing balance of RM13,000. April receipts are RM30,000 and April payments are RM40,000, which include RM20,000 for new equipment. What is the closing balance at the end of April?
prompt.ms: Bulan April bermula dengan baki akhir Mac sebanyak RM13,000. Terimaan April RM30,000 dan bayaran April RM40,000, termasuk RM20,000 untuk peralatan baharu.  Berapakah baki akhir pada penghujung April?

explanation.en: 13,000 + 30,000 − 40,000 = 3,000. This is exactly what a cash budget is for: the equipment is affordable, but only just, and one month later it would not have been.
explanation.ms: 13,000 + 30,000 − 40,000 = 3,000. Inilah tujuan sebenar belanjawan tunai: peralatan itu mampu dibeli, tetapi nyaris sahaja, dan sebulan lebih lewat ia sudah tidak mampu.

prompt.en: Every month of a cash budget is the same short column: what you started with, everything that came in, everything that went out, and what is left. The figure at the bottom becomes the figure at the top of the next month. Each rung below takes one more line away.
prompt.ms: Setiap bulan dalam belanjawan tunai ialah lajur pendek yang sama: apa yang anda mulakan, segala yang masuk, segala yang keluar, dan apa yang tinggal. Angka di bawah menjadi angka di atas bulan berikutnya. Setiap anak tangga di bawah menanggalkan satu baris lagi.

prompt.en: The workings are done. Finish the last line.
prompt.ms: Kerja kira sudah siap. Selesaikan baris terakhir.

scenario.en: March. Opening cash RM5,000. Cash sales RM12,000. Received from debtors RM24,000. Paid suppliers RM18,000. Wages RM7,000. Rent RM3,000.
scenario.ms: Mac. Tunai awal RM5,000. Jualan tunai RM12,000. Terimaan daripada penghutang RM24,000. Bayaran kepada pembekal RM18,000. Gaji RM7,000. Sewa RM3,000.

prompt.en: Three lines are missing. Complete the month.
prompt.ms: Tiga baris hilang. Lengkapkan bulan itu.

scenario.en: April. Opening cash RM8,000. Cash sales RM15,000. Received from debtors RM20,000. Paid suppliers RM22,000. Wages RM9,000. Rent RM4,000.
scenario.ms: April. Tunai awal RM8,000. Jualan tunai RM15,000. Terimaan daripada penghutang RM20,000. Bayaran kepada pembekal RM22,000. Gaji RM9,000. Sewa RM4,000.

explanation.en: 8,000 + 35,000 − 35,000 = 8,000. Receipts and payments cancelled out exactly, so the month ends where it began — a flat month is not the same as a month with nothing happening in it.
explanation.ms: 8,000 + 35,000 − 35,000 = 8,000. Terimaan dan bayaran saling membatalkan dengan tepat, jadi bulan itu berakhir di tempat ia bermula — bulan yang rata bukanlah sama dengan bulan yang tiada apa-apa berlaku.

prompt.en: Only the opening balance is given. Build the whole month.
prompt.ms: Hanya baki awal diberi. Bina keseluruhan bulan itu.

scenario.en: May. Opening cash RM3,000. Cash sales RM18,000. Received from debtors RM26,000. Paid suppliers RM25,000. Wages RM11,000. Rent RM5,000.
scenario.ms: Mei. Tunai awal RM3,000. Jualan tunai RM18,000. Terimaan daripada penghutang RM26,000. Bayaran kepada pembekal RM25,000. Gaji RM11,000. Sewa RM5,000.

explanation.en: 3,000 + 44,000 − 41,000 = 6,000. The business is solvent all month, but only because the debtors paid: without that RM26,000 it would have run out of cash.
explanation.ms: 3,000 + 44,000 − 41,000 = 6,000. Perniagaan mampu bertahan sepanjang bulan, tetapi hanya kerana penghutang membayar: tanpa RM26,000 itu ia akan kehabisan tunai.
